newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UK's Blair condemns IRA killing of N.Irish police.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair condemns IRA killing of N.Irish police.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair on Monday condemned the IRA for the murder of two policemen in Northern Ireland and said there was "no question" of further meetings with its political wing Sinn Fein.
The Irish Republican Army earlier claimed responsibility for the close-range shootings in the town of Lurgan, southwest of Belfast.

Both Britain's new Labour government and Dublin had resumed talks with Sinn Fein in recent months with the hope of bringing about a new IRA ceasefire and reaching an agreement to end Northern Ireland's 28 years of conflict.
Government officials said earlier on Monday that Britain had broken off contacts with Sinn Fein -- which seeks a united Ireland -- because of the shootings.
Blair said any further meeting with Sinn Fein was now out of the question.

"(The republicans') cynicism and hypocrisy are sickening. Their actions defy normal understanding. It is difficult to interpret this latest attack as anything but a signal that Sinn Fein and the IRA are not interested in peace and democracy," he said in a statement in Amsterdam, where he is attending a European Union summit.
"There is obviously no question of a further meeting with Sinn Fein in these circumstances."
Blair said he had been horrified by the news of the killings.

"My reaction to this outrage is the reaction of decent people everywhere -- one of horror at the act of murder and anger at what looks like a deliberate attempt to place obstacles in the road of peace."
Nevertheless, Blair said his government would not abandon its efforts to bring peace to Northern Ireland.
